nodes.label: Concentration Splitting (E_low / E_high)
nodes.rationale: Excipients behave differently at low vs. high concentrations; a simple linear input cannot capture the threshold where an excipient switches from 'shielding' to 'crowding', so numeric inputs are split into _low and _high features around domain-specific thresholds (e.g. Arginine @ 150mM).

nodes.label: Data Scarcity in High-Viscosity Regions (design challenge)
nodes.norm_label: data scarcity in high-viscosity regions (design challenge)

nodes.label: Physics-Informed Loss
nodes.rationale: Experimental data for extremely viscous samples (>50 cP) is rare and expensive to generate, yet is the critical failure mode to predict; penalty terms enforce known physical laws (e.g. shear thinning, valid input-gradient sensitivities) instead of training on MSE alone.

nodes.label: Learnable Physics Priors
nodes.rationale: Enforces known behaviors even where data is sparse by initializing network weights from textbook chemistry (Hofmeister Series, EXCIPIENT_PRIORS) rather than random noise, while still allowing a learned delta to fine-tune priors from observed data.

nodes.label: Regime Gating
nodes.rationale: The effect of an excipient (e.g. Arginine) depends entirely on the protein's surface charge and current interaction regime, so behavior is gated by the computed regime (Near/Mixed/Far).

nodes.label: Shear Thinning Constraint
nodes.rationale: Penalizes predictions where viscosity increases as shear rate increases, which is a physical impossibility for these fluids.

nodes.label: Input Gradient Constraints
nodes.rationale: Penalizes the model if it learns physically invalid sensitivities, e.g. if adding salt decreases viscosity in a regime where it is known to increase it.
